teaching_examples.text: Se munuc sealde ðæs cuman suna męte.
teaching_examples.translation: The monk gave food to the stranger’s son.
teaching_examples.target: Nested dependent genitive within a dative recipient phrase.
Dative person and genitive thing denied.
Invariant quantity word plus genitive plural.

teaching_examples.text: Ān ðāra munuca cōm tō ðǣm hūse.
teaching_examples.translation: One of the monks came to the house.
teaching_examples.target: Substantival one with genitive whole; destination dative.
The governed dative is not an accusative direct object.

teaching_examples.text: Sēo gāt is ðǣm scēaphierde behēfu.

Accusative experiencer with a third-singular impersonal verb.

compositions.title: The stranger and the monk
compositions.text: Sum cuma cōm tō ðǣm giesthūse. Hine hyngrede, and hē wæs untrum. Ān ðāra munuca geseah ðone cuman. Se munuc sealde him męte and wæter. Se cuma cwæð: “Ðū ne forwiernst mē mętes.” Se munuc cwæð: “Ic fēde ðē gōde męte.” Se cuma ǣt ðone męte and dranc ðæt wæter.
compositions.target: Connected relief of hunger: impersonal experience, partitive identification, a gift, denial contrast and instrumental means. No private full translation is included.
compositions.support_policy: All required lexical senses, forms and constructions must be productive before this independent reading.
